'''Nanubae''' (Kapagmai, Aunda) is an [[Arafundi language]] of [[Papua New Guinea]]. It is close to [[Tapei language|Tapei]]; the name ''Alfendio'' was once used for both.

==Locations==
Kassell, et al. (2018) list Imanmeri, Wambrumas, and Yamandim as the villages where Nanubae is spoken. Additionally, there are some speakers in Imboin, which also has [[Tapei language|Tapei]] speakers.<ref>Kassell, Alison, Bonnie MacKenzie and Margaret Potter. 2018. ''[https://pnglanguages.sil.org/resources/archives/74262 Three Arafundi Languages: A Sociolinguistic Profile of Andai, Nanubae, and Tapei]''. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2017-003.</ref>

According to ''[[Ethnologue]]'', it is spoken in Imanmeri ({{coord|-4.646309|143.604125|type:city_region:PG|name=Imanmeri}}), Wambrumas ({{coord|-4.726468|143.564188|type:city_region:PG|name=Wambrumas}}), and Yamandim ({{coord|-4.73418|143.611984|type:city_region:PG|name=Yamandim}}) villages of [[Karawari Rural LLG]], [[East Sepik Province]].<ref name=e25/><ref name="UN-PNG">{{cite web |url=https://data.humdata.org/dataset/village-coordinates-lookup |title=Papua New Guinea Village Coordinates Lookup |author=United Nations in Papua New Guinea |work=Humanitarian Data Exchange |version=1.31.9 |date=2018}}</ref>
